newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to ax government jobs, raise tax collection.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to ax government jobs, raise tax collection.

text.p: Brazil unveiled on Friday a package of measures to curb federal spending, eliminate government jobs and increase tax collection.
State companies will also be made to sell non-operational assets in the drive to reduce the country's fiscal deficit.
Finance Minister Pedro Malan said the package was aimed at aiding passage of constitutional reforms sitting in Congress.
"We believe this fiscal adjustment gives continuity to our efforts to approve constitutional reform in Congress, which we will not abandon," Malan told reporters.
Major reforms to Brazil's pension and tax systems and the civil service have gotten bogged down in Congress with little chance of approval until well into 1997.
Malan said the new measures could bring Brazil's deficit under 2.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997, down from an expected 3.5 percent this year and 5 percent in 1995.
More than 100,000 civil service posts will be eliminated in the federal government, and another 94,000 posts will be axed in state-owned firms.
But 2,000 new tax officials will be hired to boost the government's tax revenues and crack down on tax debtors.
